At 2 life, removing the creature that can bring back Archon of Cruelty should be the priority.

Casting Unearth before combat to return Psychic Frog, then attacking with both Emperor of Bones (4/4) and Psychic Frog (1/2) would deal exactly 5 damage for lethal, with the option to discard cards to pump Frog for overkill.

annotations.description: The opponent is at 1 life with all lands tapped. DSV3 Proud has Unearth in hand and Psychic Frog in the graveyard (mana value 2, eligible target). Casting Unearth on Psychic Frog would return it to the battlefield, and on the next turn it could attack for lethal (opponent is at 1 life). However, there's an even simpler consideration: Emperor of Bones is a 4/4 that attacked this turn, and the opponent is at 1 life. The key issue is that instead of setting up a guaranteed kill with Unearth on Psychic Frog (which would provide an additional attacker next turn), the player chose to flashback Faithless Looting, which costs 2R (requiring 3 mana) and exiles itself. Looking at available mana: Blood Crypt (untapped), Swamp (untapped), Watery Grave (untapped) = 3 mana available. Steam Vents is tapped. Flashback Faithless Looting costs {2}{R}, which requires Blood Crypt for R plus 2 more = exactly 3 mana, using all remaining mana. This means they can't also cast Unearth this turn. With the opponent at 1 life, Unearth on Psychic Frog creates a second attacker that essentially guarantees lethal next turn even if the opponent has a blocker. The Faithless Looting flashback draws 2 and discards 2 but uses all mana and doesn't directly advance the kill. That said, Emperor of Bones as a 4/4 can likely attack for lethal next turn anyway since the opponent is at 1 life - they only need to connect with anything. But Unearthing Psychic Frog gives a second threat and makes it much harder for the opponent to survive. The flashback is unnecessary card selection when the game is essentially won.
annotations.actionTaken: Flashed back Faithless Looting from the graveyard, spending all available mana on card selection
annotations.betterLine: Cast Unearth targeting Psychic Frog in the graveyard to create a second attacker, making it nearly impossible for the opponent at 1 life to survive the next combat. With Emperor of Bones already on board, two attackers against an opponent at 1 life is overwhelming.

annotations.description: Cast Prismatic Ending before playing a land drop. Should play a land first (Arena of Glory or Arid Mesa) before casting spells - standard sequencing that preserves maximum flexibility. At 1 life, having an extra land on board could matter for future turns if they survive.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Prismatic Ending before making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Arena of Glory or Arid Mesa first, then cast Prismatic Ending on Emperor of Bones

annotations.description: At 1 life, playing Arid Mesa which costs 1 life to activate means it's a completely dead land that can never produce mana. They already have one unusable fetchland (Marsh Flats) on the battlefield for the same reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Arid Mesa as their land drop, a fetchland they can never activate at 1 life.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arena of Glory, which enters untapped (they control Sacred Foundry, a Mountain) and produces R mana. This would give them 5 usable mana sources next turn to cast Quantum Riddler ({3}{U}{U}) with Hallowed Fountain and Thundering Falls providing UU.

annotations.description: At 1 life with only 6 lands (including untapped Arid Mesa, Marsh Flats, Plains, Sacred Foundry, and tapped Hallowed Fountain and Thundering Falls), GPT5m tried to cast Quantum Riddler for {3}{U}{U} but couldn't generate enough blue mana. They have Arena of Glory in hand which could have been played first as a land drop, but that only produces red. The correct play was to crack a fetchland (Marsh Flats or Arid Mesa) to get another dual land — but at 1 life, paying 1 life for a fetchland would kill them. So they're effectively stuck and can't cast Quantum Riddler this turn. The attempted cast that got rolled back wasted priority and showed the opponent information. More importantly, they should have recognized they couldn't cast it and instead played Arena of Glory as their land drop and passed, preserving any information advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Quantum Riddler but failed to complete mana payment, resulting in the spell being rolled back and no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arena of Glory as land drop and pass turn. At 1 life, fetchlands can't be cracked, so Quantum Riddler is uncastable this turn. Should have recognized this immediately rather than attempting an illegal mana payment.
